events.info: Have I Said Too Much: The Police, Hollywood, And Other Adventures. Stewart Copeland, world famous drummer, founder of the most successful rock band of the 1980s, The Police, composer of film scores, video games and operas, multi Grammy winner and Rock and Roll Hall of Famer, writer and film maker, is heading out on his first American spoken word tour, to talk about it all in his usual funny, intelligent, sharp and unique way. An evening of conversation, with photos, videos and a Q&A.
events.pleaseNote: ACCESSIBILITY - Accessible seating is available online through Ticketmaster by filtering on the ADA Icon and selecting Accessible Seats. Exceptions will be made for necessary medical equipment or accommodations.

generalInfo.generalRule: Spectrum Center is committed to creating a safe, comfortable, and enjoyable sports and entertainment experience. Guests of Spectrum Center have a right to expect an environment where guests will: • Respect and appreciate each and every fan. • Be treated in a consistent, professional and courteous manner by all arena and team personnel. • Enjoy the arena experience free from disruptive behavior, including foul or abusive language or obscene gestures. • Consume alcoholic beverages in a responsible manner. Intervention with an impaired, intoxicated or underage guest will be handled in a prompt and safe manner • Sit only in ticketed seats and show tickets when requested. • Act in an appropriate manner without fighting, throwing objects or attempting to enter the court or stage area. • Smoke in designated smoking areas only. • Wear appropriate clothing and have signage that is free of any obscene or indecent messages. • Comply with requests from arena staff regarding arena operations and emergency response procedures. The arena staff has been trained to intervene where necessary to help ensure that the above expectations are met, and guests are encouraged to report any inappropriate behavior to the nearest event staff member. Guests who choose not to adhere to these provisions will be subject to ejection without refund and revocation of tickets and may also be in violation of the law resulting in possible arrest and prosecution.
generalInfo.childRule: Children 2 years or older must have a ticket for most events at the Spectrum Center. This age restriction can fluctuate from event to event.

boxOfficeInfo.phoneNumberDetail: Box Office: 704-372-3600 (Tickets cannot be ordered over the phone. Call 800.745.3000 to purchase tickets)
boxOfficeInfo.openHoursDetail: The main box office is located on the south side of Bojangles Coliseum. Regular hours are Wednesday and Friday 10am to 5pm. Show days we open 2 hours prior to the event start time at Ovens Auditorium Box Office. Box Office hours subject to change without notice. Box Office hours subject to change without notice.
boxOfficeInfo.acceptedPaymentDetail: Cash, Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover. All credit card purchases require a matching photo ID to the ticket buyer and credit card.
boxOfficeInfo.willCallDetail: Will call orders can be picked up at the box office during normal business hours or right before the event. (Note: Certain events may not allow will call pick-up until the day of the performance.) Please bring a picture id, the credit card used to make the purchase and the order number. Tickets will only be released to the person whose name is on the account.

venues.parkingDetail: Facility parking lots are located immediately to the left after turning onto Briar Creek. Auxiliary parking lots (if needed) are located immediately to the right. ADA parking is available. For most events, parking is included in your ticket price. There are some events that is not included in your ticket. Parking fees range from $6.00 - $10.00 per vehicle.
venues.accessibleSeatingDetail: Accessible seating is available for patrons with disabilities. Tickets can be purchased through all sales channels. Those wishing to purchase accessible seats are allowed to have up to three companions sitting with them (based on availability). Ovens Auditorium strongly encourages those needing to purchase tickets in accessible seating areas to do so as far in advance as possible. All accessible seating will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. Every effort will be made on the day of an event to accommodate those needing accessible seats but are holding a ticket for a conventional seat but all such exchanges are based on availability. Accessible seats are located throughout the Orchestra (lower) Level. A wheelchair lift is also available. Ovens Auditorium has an FM amplified listening system for patron convenience. System units are available at the coat-check room in the main lobby. To obtain an Assistive Listening Device, guests must present proper identification (state ID, etc.). These devices are free of charge.

generalInfo.generalRule: Video cameras, flash cameras, laser pointers, outside food or beverage and weapons are prohibited at Ovens Auditorium. Any non-clear bag larger than 4.5" x 6.5" and clear bags larger than 12" x 6" x 12" are not allowed. These include but are not limited to: backpacks, briefcases, camera bags, cinch bags, computer bags, fanny packs, coolers of any kind and luggage of any kind. All patrons are subject to search. No re-entry. Ovens Auditorium is a smoke-free facility. Prices listed include all applicable taxes.
generalInfo.childRule: Ovens Auditorium was designed for fans of all ages. Unless otherwise noted, children 2 and over must have a purchased ticket to enter the Bojangles Entertainment Complex. Any child under the age of 2 admitted without a ticket must share a seat with an accompanying adult. Please confirm with the box office before purchasing at (704) 372-3600.
